title: Find the largest upload the gateway accepts

blocks.text: The desktop client shows "files up to N bytes" next to its upload button. Customers put different storage gateways in front of the service, each with its own size limit, so the client finds N by probing: each probe sends a request of one size to the gateway's test endpoint, which accepts it or refuses it. A gateway that accepts a size accepts every smaller one. Probes are slow, so the client can afford a few dozen of them, and some gateways are configured with a ceiling of `Integer.MAX_VALUE` bytes.

Write `largestAccepted(maxBytes, accepts)` in `src/main/java/practice/UploadLimit.java`: the largest size in `1..maxBytes` that the gateway accepts, or `0` when it refuses even one byte. Probe only sizes in that range. About eight lines.
This is the mirror of a search for the first bad build: here the answer is the last size that passes.

cases.says: a gateway that refuses even one byte gives 0
the search ends on the largest accepted size; a midpoint that can equal the bound it moves stalls on the last two candidates
with a range that reaches Integer.MAX_VALUE, every probe stays inside the range
the loop condition matches the updates, so the search stops once a single candidate is left

origin.section: The Invariant Decides the Condition, the Updates and the Midpoint

concepts: A binary search's invariant decides its condition, its updates and which way its midpoint rounds; the midpoint is computed so that it can't overflow.
